heard: An asteroid flew closer to Earth than the space station. It skimmed just 230 miles above the South Pacific. This is the closest near miss ever documented. It beat the previous record by over 1500 miles, but every telescope on Earth was completely blind to it. The rock approached from the sun, hiding in the glare. Astronomers only spotted it 15 hours after it passed. Earth's gravity hijacked the rock and shrank its orbit. On that Friday the 13th, the world never saw it coming.
